aoi.description: Western India / Arabian Sea ecological AOI

buffer_note: [PROJECT-DEFINED] 50 km buffer chosen to capture edge receptors within realistic 24-hour Oil Spread V2 drift range. Derived from drift.py WIND_LEEWAY=0.03, Arabian Sea typical surface current ~0.8 m/s → max realistic 24h drift ~108 km; 50 km = ~46% of that. Physical spread radius (<2 km) and diffusion sigma (<2 km) are negligible by comparison.

coastline.reference: Natural Earth. Free vector and raster map data @ naturalearthdata.com
coastline.phase_note: Phase 2 acquired and clipped base coastline geometry (MultiLineString). Phase 3 segments, buffers, and classifies sensitive coastline receptors.

segmentation.rationale: Balances spatial resolution against receptor count. Avoids thousands of tiny fragments while providing meaningful coastline sections for exposure assessment.

buffering.method: Projected CRS (EPSG:32643 / UTM 43N) for metric accuracy, reprojected to EPSG:4326 for storage
buffering.rationale: Represents sensitive coastal zone extent for oil-shoreline interaction assessment.

proximity_classification.method: PostGIS ST_DWithin with geography cast for metric distance
proximity_classification.rationale: Captures direct coastal adjacency plus minor positional errors in receptor datasets. This is NOT a scientifically validated exposure zone; it is an operational classification rule.

sensitivity_tiers.medium: Near MPA only, no mangrove/coral association (within 2 km)
sensitivity_tiers.low: No ecological receptor association within 2 km
sensitivity_tiers.priority: HIGH > MEDIUM > LOW (segment near both mangrove and MPA remains HIGH)

limitations: Classification is operationally defined for V1 oil-spill response prioritization
Not a universal scientific coastline sensitivity standard
Proximity-based association does not model hydrodynamic connectivity or ecological vulnerability gradients
Natural Earth 10m resolution may miss small embayments or coastal features
Fixed 5 km segmentation may group heterogeneous coastline sections
Receptor datasets have their own coverage gaps and positional uncertainties

gmw.sensitivity_tier_note: high — mangroves are IUCN-recognised highly sensitive coastal habitats

wdpa.dataset_name: WDPA — World Database on Protected Areas (India, Sep-2026)
wdpa.reference: UNEP-WCMC and IUCN (2026). Protected Planet: The World Database on Protected Areas. Cambridge UK / Gland Switzerland.
wdpa.license: CC-BY for non-commercial/research use. See https://www.protectedplanet.net/en/legal
wdpa.geographic_coverage: India national coverage (IND shapefile, clipped to AOI+buffer)
wdpa.acquisition_method: Direct download from Protected Planet CloudFront CDN (public IND package)
wdpa.marine_filter: REALM in ['Coastal','Marine'] OR GIS_M_AREA > 0 (Sep-2026 IND package uses REALM not MARINE)
wdpa.coverage_gap_note: India's WDPA IND polygon package has limited offshore marine PA coverage. Only Thane Creek (coastal) is present in the AOI+buffer for Sep-2026. India designates many marine areas as Wildlife Sanctuaries under domestic law but these may not all appear in the WDPA polygon layer. This is a known WDPA data limitation, not a processing error.

aca.dataset_name: UNEP-WCMC Global Distribution of Coral Reefs 2018 v4.1
aca.preferred_source_status: INACCESSIBLE — ACA website returns HTTP 403 for programmatic requests; GEE asset requires authenticated session. UNEP-WCMC v4.1 used as documented fallback per project scope.
aca.reference: UNEP-WCMC, WorldFish Centre, WRI, TNC (2018). Global distribution of coral reefs, compiled from multiple sources including the Millennium Coral Reef Mapping Project.
aca.license: Non-commercial use with attribution required. See https://wcmc.io/WCMC_008
aca.acquisition_method: Direct download from WCMC S3 (via wcmc.io/WCMC_008 redirect)
aca.coverage_note: Arabian Sea has limited coral extent. Expected sites in AOI: Malvan Marine Sanctuary (~16°N 73.5°E), Gulf of Kutch (~22-23°N 68-70°E). Zero or few features is scientifically plausible, not a processing error.
aca.sensitivity_tier_note: high — coral reefs are IUCN-recognised highly sensitive habitats
